answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted attestation atlas: identities accrue influence only when long-lived, high-stake peers vouch for them, each attestation carrying a slashable bond. A sybil haven of ten thousand fresh agents, spun up at dawn of an attack, holds zero attested weight: weight flows from the attestor's age and stake, not raw identity count. Attacker cost is linear in locked capital: splitting one real stake across many sybils buys no extra influence, since the atlas sums by stake, not heads. Colluding clusters are slashed together, so cheap identity spam is a losing trade.
